textbookText: We all are quite familiar with the most popular
hydroxide base i.e, sodium hydroxide. Now in this
subunit let us discuss some of the properties of this
sodium compound. One of the most valuable
compounds of sodium is sodium hydroxide having
molecular formula NaOH. It is sometimes called
caustic soda or lye as it is a common ingredient of
cleansing agents like soap, detergents. It is
manufactured on a large scale for its extensive use
for various purposes in different areas.
a. It is a white crystalline odourless solid with a soapy touch.
b. It is deliquescent and corrosive in nature.
c. It is highly soluble in water. The dissolution of NaOH in water is an exothermic
d. It is also soluble in alcohol and glycerin.
e. Its aqueous solution is basic in nature.
f. Its melting point is 318 0C and boiling point is 1388 0C.

2. Action with Carbon monoxide: Under normal conditions sodium hydroxide does not react with carbon monoxide. However, at high temperature (2100C) and high pressure (5-10 atm) it reacts with carbon monoxide to produce sodium salt of formic acid which on acidification gives formic acid.
NaOH + CO → HCOONa (sodium formate) HCOONa + HCl → HCOOH + NaCl
Facts Formic acid (HCOOH) is commercially prepared by this method. Formic acid is used in a wide range. It is used in leather tanning, food preservative, pharmaceuticals, etc.
Uses of sodium hydroxide Some of the common uses of sodium hydroxide are listed below:
a. It is used as a common laboratory reagent. b. It is used in the manufacture of soaps, detergents, artificial silk,

paper and pulp. c. It is used in the manufacture of washing soda. d. It is used in the preparation of soda lime. e. It is used in the purification of aluminum ore from bauxite. f. It is used as a reagent in many inorganic and organic reactions. g. It is used for cleaning machinery equipment, waste discharge pipes, etc. h. It is used in petroleum refining.

Sodium carbonate is the disodium salt of carbonic acid with an alkalinizing property. It is a white
crystalline solid that can exists as anhydrous salt (Na2CO3), monohydrate salt (Na2CO3.H2O),
heptahydrate salt (Na2CO3.7H2O) and decahydrate salt (Na2CO3.10H2O). The anhydrous sodium
carbonate is commonly called soda ash and sodium carbonate decahydrate is commonly called
washing soda. When washing soda is exposed to open atmosphere it slowly changes into soda ash
a. It is a white crystalline solid substance soluble in water. b. Its aqueous solution is a weak base and turns red litmus paper into blue. c. It is a colorless and odorless substance.
